text:
sana: Heads-up — starting ~00:20 UTC we see a spike in NVidia Xid 48s on the eu-west1 A10 embedder fleet. Noticed across 3 racks, ~12 cards reporting transient ECC/PCI errors. Sample from logs:
```
[2024-04-05T00:22:11Z] GPU0: Xid 48: ecc_uncorrectable, GPU 0, PID 3245 (embedder-worker)
[2024-04-05T00:22:12Z] GPU2: Xid 48: pcie_uncorr, GPU 2, PID 3291
```
sana: Also seeing slight tail latency increase (p50 unchanged, p95 up ~120ms) for embedder-large. Could be retry amplification.
Liam: On it. Is this correlated to any deploy or config change?
sana: No deploys in the window per deploy-bot. Kernel/drivers look unchanged (530.41). No recent firmware updates.
maria: Can you paste the NVML dump for one affected host?
sana: Pasting excerpt:
```
# nvidia-smi -q -d ECC
GPU 0
    ECC Errors
        Volatile: Single-bit: 0, Double-bit: 1
        Aggregate: Single-bit: 12, Double-bit: 3
```
sana: PromQL to find spread: `sum by(pod) (increase(gpu_xid_errors_total[1h]))` shows most hits from pods labelled app=embedder-large and some from batch-prep.
josh: Do we have recent thermal or power warnings on those racks? I scanned node-exporter, temps normal (65C). No NVLink flaps in the NIC logs.
Liam: Could be a workload pattern hitting a kernel bug on A10 decode path. Any unusual sequence lengths or tokenization?
maria: I sampled request traces — heavier prefix reuse with KV cache on. That could interact with driver memory paths.
Liam: Quick triage plan: 1) soft-drain affected cards, 2) shift embedder-large to eu-west3 burst pool, 3) collect full nv-host logs + dmesg + driver trace, 4) open vendor ticket if we see double-bit ECC increases.
sana: Agreed. I started soft-drain on two nodes (softdrain -> graceful-term pv). infra-bot: initiated soft-drain on node-a10-34 and node-a10-37 :white_check_mark:
infra-bot: moved 8 pods off node-a10-34, 10 pods off node-a10-37.
josh: Are we OK on capacity if we shift to eu-west3? eu-west3 has lower reserved commit so cost may increase if sustained.
maria: We can burst for now; if it persists we escalate and schedule replacements. Cost impact estimate: ~+12% embedding spend for the day if we use on-demand eu-west3.
Liam: Meanwhile collect memory poison stats and NVidia diag: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.total,memory.used,driver_version --format=csv` and `dmesg | grep -i nvrm`
sana: Will attach the collected artifacts to the incident ticket. Also adding a short-term alert: increase gpu_xid_48_rate > 3/min for host group -> postpager.
maria: If we see double-bit ECC counts increasing on a per-GPU basis, we should schedule immediate hardware replacement (unsafe to keep). Single-bit can often be scrubbed but double-bit indicates failing DIMM/PCB.
josh: For the immediate runbook: - Continue soft-drain for nodes with >5 Xid48/hour - Reboot only if soft-drain doesn't clear within 30m - If double-bit ECC observed, block scheduling and open replacement order with vendor (warranty)
Liam: I’ll run a controlled repro workload on an isolated node in staging to see if we can trigger it. If stable we can rule out model-side pattern.
sana: Note — earlier we saw a similar pattern in us-west2 but it was Xid13 related to decode race; different signature here (ECC/PCI). Documenting differences in the ticket.
maria: Adding a short snippet to the alert playbook with a Prometheus query and LogQL filter for the triage: `sum by (gpu_id) (increase(gpu_xid_errors{code="48"}[10m])) > 0` and `|~ "Xid 48"` in logs.
josh: Who owns the replacement procurement? CC @maria.
maria: I'll coordinate with hardware-ops. If vendor RMA -> we'll schedule node cordon+replace, no need for whole-rack drain unless multiple cards fail.
sana: OK wrapping up: soft-drain active, pods migrated, extra alerting, Liam will run repro, Maria handles procurement if hw-level fails. I’ll update the ticket with NVML dumps and dmesg in 15m. :thumbsup:
Liam: Thanks — keep updates here.
